mainEntity.name: Does weight loss diet will weaken my immunity?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is only a myth. An unhealthy diet and excess body fat weaken your immune system. Even modest weight loss reverses many of the damaging changes often seen in the immune cells of obese individuals. Whichever diet you choose, our goal is to balance your system. We provide you variety of fruits, vegetables, legumes, nuts, and seeds in your plan which are very essential for strengthening your immune system. Following a crash diet or fad diet to lose weight quickly is extremely harmful and may weaken your immune system. These diets are deficient in essential nutrients, especially proteins, vitamins, and minerals, needed for the efficient response of our immune system. So it is always recommended to follow a diet under the guidance of a certified Dietician.

mainEntity.name: Are there certain ages at which a body's metabolism slows down?

acceptedAnswer.text: Study published in August 2021 in Science suggests that differences in metabolism is based on four distinct periods of life: From infancy to 1 year old, metabolic rate surged until it was about 50 percent higher than it will be during adulthood. From 1 to 20 years old, metabolism decreased by almost 3 percent a year. From 20 to 60, metabolism didn't change. After age 60, metabolism decreased by 0.7 percent annually.

mainEntity.name: How is a dietician different from nutritionists?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dietician has had 5 years of accredited university training specifically around nutrition science. We use food more than we would ever use supplements. Our recommendations are science-based rather than the latest trends in dieting and eating. A dietician can also call themselves a nutritionist however a nutritionist cannot call themselves a dietician.
